analysis: The experiment cleanly tested the hypothesis that adding train-only user-author, user-video, and user-tab affinity count features to the fixed item/context LambdaRank feature set would improve personalized ranking. The trusted outcome does not support that claim: standalone validation primary changed by -0.00014599092509692824 with a 95% paired CI of [-0.0011861589289728525, 0.0009444088297450523], which includes zero, and the portfolio comparison was also negative (-0.0002527445864699551) with a CI including zero. Predictions did change across seeds, so the feature addition was active, but any effect was too small and directionally unfavorable on average. Diagnostic slices also fail to support the expected benefit on lower-popularity items: all train_item_popularity_quartiles were slightly negative, and high-history users and several tabs, especially tab 6, degraded. There were a few positive slices for low-history and medium-history users, but they were not strong or consistent enough to overcome the overall null-to-negative result.
next_lesson: Naive train-only pair-count affinity features are too sparse or redundant here; next personalization attempt should use a stronger backoff design rather than raw user-item/video memorization counts.
